claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the Nikon D3400 body.
Photo 1 shows the Nikon DX AF-P 70-300mm lens barrel.
Static photos cannot verify mechanical or electronic operation.
Photo 2 shows the rubber grip is heavily worn and peeling.
Photo 0 and Photo 1 confirm the Nikon branding.

risks.risk: High shutter count indicating heavy professional use or near-failure.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the shutter count from a tool like 'CameraShutterCount' using the last JPEG taken.
risks.if_unproven: as having a very high shutter count near the end of its rated life.

risks.risk: Internal lens fungus or scratches affecting image quality.
risks.proof: A clear photo looking through the lens elements with a light source behind them.
risks.if_unproven: as having optical defects requiring professional cleaning.

risks.risk: Sensor damage or permanent dust spots.
risks.proof: A photo of a plain white wall or sky taken at a high aperture (e.g., f/22).
risks.if_unproven: as having a dirty or scratched sensor.

risks.risk: LCD screen damage or dead pixels.
risks.proof: A photo of the rear LCD screen powered on and displaying a menu.
risks.if_unproven: as having a non-functional or damaged display.

risks.risk: Missing essential accessories like battery and charger.
risks.proof: A photo showing the camera battery and the specific Nikon charger.
risks.if_unproven: as body and lens only, requiring separate purchase of power accessories.

proof_requests: Photos of the lens glass (front and back) and looking through the barrel.
Photo of the rear LCD screen while the camera is turned on.
Photo of the sensor with the lens removed.
Photo of the battery and charger.
response.reason: The camera and lens models are clearly identified, allowing for a valuation based on the observed heavy wear on the grip and the worst-case assumption for unverified internal components.
